inputs.name: langfuse_version
inputs.description: Tag of the docker.io/langfuse/langfuse and docker.io/langfuse/langfuse-worker images, such as "4.72.0". Change web_image_digest and worker_image_digest with it.

inputs.name: web_image_digest
inputs.description: Digest of docker.io/langfuse/langfuse for langfuse_version. Podman pulls by the digest, so a tag that moves upstream can't change what runs.

inputs.name: worker_image_digest
inputs.description: Digest of docker.io/langfuse/langfuse-worker for langfuse_version.

inputs.name: clickhouse_version
inputs.description: Tag of the docker.io/clickhouse/clickhouse-server image, such as "26.8.36.3". Langfuse 4 needs ClickHouse 25.12 or later. Change clickhouse_image_digest with it.

inputs.name: clickhouse_image_digest
inputs.description: Digest of docker.io/clickhouse/clickhouse-server for clickhouse_version.

inputs.name: minio_image_digest
inputs.description: Digest of cgr.dev/chainguard/minio:latest to run. Chainguard's free tier publishes only the latest tag, so the digest is the pin.

inputs.name: public_url
inputs.description: The address people and SDKs reach Langfuse at, such as "https://langfuse.example.com". Langfuse sets it as NEXTAUTH_URL and builds sign-in redirects and links from it.

inputs.name: database_url
inputs.description: PostgreSQL connection URI, such as "postgresql://langfuse:PASSWORD@127.0.0.1:5432/langfuse". It reaches the host in a root-only file and never the plan or state.

inputs.name: redis_url
inputs.description: Redis or Valkey URL, such as "redis://:PASSWORD@127.0.0.1:6379". The server needs maxmemory-policy noeviction. It reaches the host in a root-only file and never the plan or state.

inputs.name: organization
inputs.description: ID and name of the organization Langfuse creates on its first start, such as "homelab".

inputs.name: project
inputs.description: ID and name of the project Langfuse creates in that organization, such as "chatbot".

inputs.name: admin_email
inputs.description: Email address of the first user, who owns the organization and signs in with admin_password.

inputs.name: admin_password
inputs.description: Password of the first user. It reaches the host in a root-only file and never the plan or state. Langfuse sets it only when it creates the user.

inputs.name: project_public_key
inputs.description: Public API key Langfuse gives the project, such as "pk-lf-...". Set it with project_secret_key, or leave both null and create keys in the web interface.

inputs.name: project_secret_key
inputs.description: Secret API key that goes with project_public_key, such as "sk-lf-...".

inputs.name: signup
inputs.description: Let anyone who can reach Langfuse create an account. Off by default, so only the first user and the people they invite get in.

inputs.name: listen_address
inputs.description: Address the Langfuse web server listens on. The default keeps it on the host for a reverse proxy in front; "0.0.0.0" listens on every address.

inputs.name: port
inputs.description: Port the Langfuse web server listens on.

inputs.name: min_memory_mb
inputs.description: Memory, in MiB, a host needs before the circuit configures it. The whole stack wants 4 GB; a 4 GB host reports a little less.

inputs.name: environment
inputs.description: More of Langfuse's environment variables for the web and worker containers, such as { SMTP_CONNECTION_URL = "smtps://...", EMAIL_FROM_ADDRESS = "langfuse@example.com" }. They go in root-only files and never reach the plan or state.
